reasons.reason: Basic, the plan on the sticker price, includes zero staff accounts — hiring one part-time employee already means paying for Grow just to give them a login.

picks.why: Staff get ordinary WordPress user accounts, and the Shop Manager role grants full store access with no per-account fee and no plan tier gating it.

Core, its cheapest unlimited-contributor plan at $39 a month, and every plan above it remove the contributor cap entirely, with no staff-account limit to hit again as the team grows, unlike Grow's cap of 5 or Advanced's cap of 15.

reasons.reason: Pay with anything other than Shopify Payments and Shopify adds its own cut on top of the processor's fee — 2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, 0.6% on Advanced — for as long as that gateway stays connected.

picks.why: Charges no extra fee for using a third-party gateway; its own comparison table lists that additional fee as 'None,' and you can run several gateways at once.
Takes no percentage of sales on any plan, from $97 a month; card payments run through Stripe or its own Payments AI gateway at the standard rate with no separate markup layered on top.

reasons.reason: What you're actually selling is a course, a coaching program or a membership, not a catalog of physical items to browse.

picks.why: Bundles courses, coaching, community and checkout into one subscription with 0% platform revenue share on every plan, from $179 a month on Basic.
Sells funnels, courses and email in the same flat plan, from $17 a month on Startup, also at 0% transaction fees.

reasons.reason: You're mostly billing for appointments and services, not running a browsable product catalog.

picks.why: Built-in invoicing and scheduling live on the same $25-a-month Basic subscription as the website, with no separate Squarespace fee added to an invoice.
Its booking calendar is bundled into the same account as the funnels and email a service business would already need, not sold as a separate app.

reasons.reason: You want to own the code and hosting outright, and don't want any platform holding a cut of what you sell, on principle rather than over one bill.

picks.why: The core plugin costs $0 with 0% revenue share, and you choose, and can switch, the host and payment gateway at any time; nothing about the storefront itself is Shopify's to hold.

reasons.reason: Shopify's only $0 plan, Agentic, can't publish an online store or take an order through its checkout — there's no way to run an actual live storefront on Shopify for free.

picks.why: Its Free plan is a genuine $0 live storefront: build a funnel with a real checkout and take orders with no credit card required, until its lifetime-sales cap kicks in.
